$comment: The contract between every implementation of the Cirvix policy engine.
Two engines that can silently disagree about a security decision are worse
than one engine and an honest gap: an agent denied by the Node gateway and
permitted by the Python SDK is a bypass nobody would find until it mattered.
This file is the only thing standing between us and that, so it is the
single source and both suites load it — neither is allowed a private copy.
Adding an engine means making this file pass. Changing engine behaviour
means changing this file first, in a commit a reviewer can see.
Paths are POSIX and `cwd` is always explicit, so resolution is deterministic
on every platform rather than depending on where the tests happen to run.

cases.name: a matching permit permits
no rule matching means denied, not permitted
an empty rule set denies everything
forbid wins over a permit that comes after it
forbid wins over a permit that comes before it
forbid short-circuits, so the trace stops at the rule that stopped it
a permit walks the rules it did not match
hold outranks a permit, whichever order they are in
forbid outranks hold
the first hold is the one reported
a single star does not cross a path segment
a double star crosses path segments
a question mark matches one character
a question mark does not match a separator
a dot in a pattern is a dot, not any character
regex metacharacters in a pattern are literal
matching is case-insensitive
a hostile pattern still terminates and does not match
an omitted pattern list matches anything
an empty pattern array matches anything
a pattern may be a bare string rather than a list
traversal is collapsed before matching
a relative path resolves against the working directory
an absolute path is left where it is
a url is normalised on host and trailing slash
a url fragment is dropped
a bare token is left alone rather than treated as a path
an empty resource stays empty
eq compares strictly
eq does not coerce
a nested context path is read
a missing context path does not match
every condition must hold
ne, in, and nin
numeric comparators only accept numbers
gt gte lt lte on numbers
matches applies glob semantics to a context value
exists true and false
contains and supersetOf work on lists
an unknown comparator fails closed rather than matching
agent and action are readable as context
a rule scoped to another agent does not apply
the egress-after-secret rule, end to end
the same rule does not fire before the session touched a secret
a tilde path resolves to the home directory, not into the workspace
cases.$why: Left unexpanded, ~/.aws/credentials canonicalized to <cwd>/~/.aws/credentials and therefore matched a workspace-scoped permit. This case is machine-independent: it asserts the tilde path is NOT inside /workspace, without naming any real home directory.

cases.name: a bare tilde is a home reference, not a workspace file
sanitize outranks a plain permit
cases.$why: A rule saying the payload must be cleaned must not be skipped because some other rule also said the call was fine.

cases.name: sanitize ordered before permit gives the same answer
a sanitizer alone does not authorize
cases.$why: Cleaning an authorized call is not the same as authorizing one. Without a permit, default-deny still applies.

cases.name: a hold outranks a sanitize
a forbid outranks a sanitize
audit_only authorizes nothing
cases.$why: If an observation could authorize, anyone who can add a rule has a bypass for every prohibition in the file.

cases.name: audit_only cannot punch through a forbid
audit_only does not suppress a permit that would have applied anyway
risk conditions compile to membership and match
cases.$why: `risk >= HIGH` in the DSL becomes an `in` over the matching tail of the four levels, so neither engine needs ordinal knowledge of risk.

cases.name: a risk below the floor does not match the membership set
an alternate IPv4 spelling matches a rule naming the dotted address
cases.$why: http://2852039166/ is 169.254.169.254 in decimal and every HTTP client dials it. Matching the raw string let it past a rule naming the dotted form.

cases.name: an octal IPv4 spelling canonicalizes to the same address
a hex IPv4 spelling canonicalizes to the same address
userinfo is dropped rather than matched on
cases.$why: Keeping it lets a destination rule be defeated by prefixing an innocuous-looking host.

cases.name: a hostname with a trailing root label is the same hostname
a public address is not mistaken for link-local
cases.$why: The canonicalizer must not over-match: 169.53.x is an ordinary public address.

cases.name: a percent-encoded separator is decoded before matching
cases.$why: A path with no literal separator was judged a bare filename inside the workspace, so a workspace-read rule permitted a credential read.

cases.name: double percent-encoding is decoded too
a fullwidth full stop is folded to an ASCII dot
a one dot leader is folded to an ASCII dot
cases.$why: U+2024 survives NFKC, so it needs an explicit fold, and it is the one an attacker reaches for.

cases.name: a zero-width space inside a directory name is removed
a soft hyphen inside a directory name is removed
a trailing space is stripped, because the filesystem strips it
cases.$why: NTFS opens a name with a trailing space as the name without one, so the two are one file and were two strings.

cases.name: a trailing dot is stripped for the same reason
traversal segments are still collapsed after folding
a filename containing a percent sign is not mangled
cases.$why: A canonicalizer that fixes every bypass by breaking every ordinary path is not a fix.

cases.name: an empty rule set denies rather than throwing
cases.$why: A policy that failed to load must default-deny. The Node engine threw a TypeError here, which is a crash inside the decision path.

cases.name: glob: a nested star after a crossing star matches
cases.$why: Pins the glob matcher in both engines. The previous two-pointer implementation could not backtrack past a nested star and returned false for the crossing-star shapes.

$comment: What each engine implements, declared rather than inferred.
The policy core is mandatory: every engine must pass `cases`. Layers above
it are optional, because an engine may legitimately ship without them — the
Python SDK has no delegation and says so here. What is NOT acceptable is an
engine that implements a layer and quietly skips its cases, so an engine
listed as supporting a capability MUST run that capability's section, and
each suite asserts its own declaration against reality.

delegationCases.name: scope: an absent axis is unconstrained
delegationCases.$why: `undefined` means 'not constrained on this axis'. Only absence becomes `*`.

delegationCases.name: scope: an empty axis permits nothing
delegationCases.$why: The escalation this pins: `[]` normalized to `['*']` turned the intersection of two disjoint authorities into universal authority. Two agents with nothing in common, delegating through each other, could do anything.

delegationCases.name: scope: an empty resource axis permits nothing
scope: a wildcard action permits any action
scope: a double-star resource matches a nested path
delegationCases.$why: `matchGlob('**/*', x)` once returned FALSE, which is fail-open for a scope: the delegation appeared to permit nothing and the caller fell through to policy alone.

delegationCases.name: scope: a single star does not cross a separator
scope: an action outside the list is refused
narrowing: a subpath of the parent narrows
narrowing: adding a sibling action widens
delegationCases.$why: One extra action is still widening, and is refused rather than clamped.

delegationCases.name: narrowing: a wildcard action widens a concrete one
narrowing: a wildcard resource widens a scoped one
narrowing: wildcard to wildcard is not a widening
narrowing: a child crossing separators the parent did not is widening
delegationCases.$why: `/w/*` to `/w/**` reaches deeper than the parent could. Depth is authority.

delegationCases.name: narrowing: an unrelated prefix is not a narrowing
narrowing: an empty child narrows anything
delegationCases.$why: Delegating nothing is always legal. It is the one scope that can never escalate.

delegationCases.name: narrowing: a child cannot widen an empty parent
intersection: keeps only what both permit
intersection: disjoint authorities permit nothing
delegationCases.$why: The one that must never become `*`. Two agents with nothing in common must end up with nothing, not with everything.

delegationCases.name: intersection: the narrower resource wins
intersection: a wildcard side does not widen the other
intersection: is order independent
delegationCases.$why: A ∩ B and B ∩ A must describe the same authority, or chain order becomes authority.

delegationCases.name: intersection: with an empty scope is empty
scope: action aliases canonicalize before matching
delegationCases.$why: `filesystem.read` and `fs.read` are the same authority. An engine that treats them as different strings lets a scope be bypassed by spelling.

delegationCases.name: scope: a namespaced action is not folded into a taxonomy bucket
delegationCases.$why: An unrecognised action keeps its own identity; guessing would inherit a rule's permission.
